**Finding submitted: `missing` (TRANSITION), confidence 0.72.**

What I found:

- **Art. XIV runs only against us.** Section 14.2(a) obligates Ono to continue Clinical Studies (i), keep distributing during the Wind-down Period (ii), assign Regulatory Filings and Marketing Approvals and hand over all Data and Ono Know-How (iii), cooperate on transition and give up customer lists/data (iv), grant licenses (v), return/destroy Array's Confidential Information and Product Materials (vi), assign trademarks and domains (vii), and assign Sublicensee contracts (viii).
- **No reciprocal obligation on Array.** Nothing requires Array to provide transition assistance to us, to return/delete our Confidential Information or Data (Art. X has no return-or-destroy mechanic at all), or to certify deletion.
- **Supply gap during wind-down.** We must keep distributing under 14.2(a)(ii), but Article IX is not listed in the Section 14.5 survival clause, so Array's supply obligations arguably lapse at termination.

Redline (validated `ok:true`): new Section 14.2(a)(x) inserted after p0667 — up to six (6) months' transition assistance at Array's then-current rates, continued supply of Materials for as long as we must distribute, return of our Confidential Information and Data within thirty (30) days in a machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter — expressly subject to Array's retained rights under 14.2(a)(iii), (v) and (ix) so the existing bargain on Product Data transfer is untouched. Fallback of 90 days' assistance flagged in the comment.
